Follow.check: Seek: a seeked frame that differs from the played one fails, so a Follow must draw from its sampled value alone

Machine.check: Machines: every state its events reach is drawn and fails if it collides, has a label under 14 px, has no description, does not show its state or is described like another

MathTex.check: Glyphs: a formula the lettering snapshot does not hold fails every command

Mobject.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

Scene.check: Seek, Trace, Hold: every scenario is played and seeked; a seeked frame or trace that differs from the played one, or a picture that changes after its caption's hold begins, fails

Text.check: Text, Legibility, Glyphs: native text that overlaps other text, reads under 14 px at 1280 px, or has characters the fonts cannot draw fails

Transform.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingShapes.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingText.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

View.check: Views: at the end of every step, a view whose words, parts, boxes or opacity differ from a fresh draw of the state, placed where a sync would put it, fails

choreograph.check: Machines: an authored transition that breaks an invariant on the way, or does not end on the pictures of the state it reaches, fails

matchByKey.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

refuse.check: Machines: a bound that stops an event the model refuses anyway fails

view.check: Views: at the end of every step, a view whose words, parts, boxes or opacity differ from a fresh draw of the state, placed where a sync would put it, fails

Card.check: Views: a card drawn from state is compared part by part, its lit row included, with a fresh draw

CodeBlock.check: Views: a code panel drawn from state is compared part by part, its focus bar included, with a fresh draw

Diagram.check: Routes over labels, Legibility: an imported connector over label ink, or an imported label under 14 px in its viewport, fails

stage.check: Words, Step change: a kept drawing with no text and no describe, or a step whose resting picture equals the previous step's, fails

stagedStep.check: Staged steps: a step redrawn from the state its trace recorded that differs, or whose draw ignores its state, fails

depthOrder.check: Invariants: registered with addInvariant, it fails on the first frame that draws a piece out of depth order

keyed.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

keyedParts.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

legend.check: Looks: a caption or line naming a colour or pattern that no word on the stage says fails; a legend that keys the look answers it

table.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

features.uses: `TransformMatchingText`, `TransformMatchingShapes` (`shapeKey()`), `TransformMatching` with your own key or `matchByKey()` (keyed components); `summary()`, `pairs`, `removed`, `added`
`new TransformDiff(before, after, { hunks })` and its `plan`; `diffLines`, `parseUnifiedDiff` for hunks

features.feature: Parts of a line of code

examples.explaining: Two algorithms or policies on the same input
examples.shows: One card with a column per policy, read from the model's trace; one scenario that favours each policy; captions tested against the model

examples.explaining: A code change and what it does to a system
examples.shows: `TransformDiff` on the code, the same edit replayed on the diagram with `ops`, a setting for hit or miss

examples.explaining: Authoring feature reference
examples.shows: Choose a feature scenario: the recipe step shows the author-written API, the result step runs it. See [scope and specialized APIs](../../docs/FEATURE-TOUR.md)

examples.explaining: A protocol or request flow
examples.shows: A sequence diagram revealed message by message (`build: 'frame'`, `reveal`); a setting that adds the attacker's step

examples.explaining: A sequence of separate pictures, one per step
examples.shows: `s.steps([...])`: each step carries its `state` and a `draw(state, s)` for its picture; `rayner check` redraws every step after the run and fails one that comes out different

examples.explaining: A data structure changing step by step
examples.shows: No diagram: native shapes drawn as views of `scene.state`, a `Machine` of push and pop, each event's motion authored with the transition's `t.choreograph`, `Follow` for the pointers

examples.explaining: A state machine
examples.shows: A state diagram driven by the real reducer as a `Machine`, code spans boxed from the row it read

examples.explaining: A model the reader could drive with events
examples.shows: A `Machine` over the model's step, refusals with reasons, a live last step; `rayner check` draws every reachable state

examples.explaining: Nested or parallel states
examples.start: A Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` with composites and regions ([recipe](../../docs/REFERENCE.md#state-machines-and-graphs)); `statecharts` when position carries meaning
examples.shows: `statecharts`: native boxes and arrows drawn from a model's states and transitions; a keyed `view` whose parts keep their identity as a grid becomes regions; a flat and a structured drawing side by side

examples.explaining: A race or ordering bug
examples.shows: A real controlled-promise run that opens on the unguarded race (the page ends on the older query) before naming the ticket that fixes it; guard and completion order change the displayed result

examples.explaining: A rate or a model's numbers over time
examples.shows: `token-bucket`: `Axes`, `lineGraph`, `Follow` for the gauge and the line from one elapsed time; `seasons`: `Axes.plot`; a setting that reruns the model

examples.explaining: Identity, hashing or text that changes
examples.shows: `exgit`: Git's objects drawn as `view`s of the repository's state and synced as each command runs, a `BraceLabel` on the abbreviated id; `glyph`: `TransformMatchingShapes` pairs letters by their outlines

examples.explaining: Keyed cells or nodes rearranged between pictures of the same state
examples.shows: `view(...).sync({ match: 'key' })`; `matchByKey({ fallback })` for unkeyed parts that should stay put, `{ text: 'whole' }` when a relabelled part is a new thing (`statecharts`); `find(key)` to address a part

examples.explaining: A real tool's behaviour, checked against it
examples.shows: A model checked against the tool's own output, with a fidelity test

examples.explaining: Records, schedules or shares
examples.shows: Diagram families beyond flowcharts

examples.explaining: A subject in another language
examples.shows: `meta.lang: 'fr'`; descriptions in French

examples.explaining: A drawing made by hand, values said on it
examples.shows: `s.sketch` with a pen and pencil, `s.focus` on the camera, `s.carry`, `s.dimension` and `s.callout` instead of cards
